projects.title: Projects
projects.p1_desc: PowerApps + SharePoint app that allows each employee to access only the protocols assigned to their role and department.
projects.p1_why: I learned to integrate different tools into a coherent flow that automates tasks and reduces manual errors—my first step towards a “complete solution”.
projects.p1_problem: Employees needed to quickly reach the right protocol (and the current version) without manual searching through documents.
projects.p1_solution: PowerApps connected to SharePoint with role/department filtering, search, version control and read tracking.
projects.p1_result: Evidence: real project (final project) with role-based filtering and read/version traceability.
projects.p2_desc: Desktop catalog with full CRUD: add, update, delete, filter and sort products across multiple screens.
projects.p2_why: It helped me structure data in a desktop app and keep consistency across screens—solid foundations for bigger projects.
projects.p2_problem: I wanted to practice a complete desktop catalog app with navigation, persistence and typical CRUD + filtering flows.
projects.p2_solution: C#/.NET app with Avalonia UI (MVVM) and JSON persistence, including search/filter and basic CRUD.
projects.p2_result: Evidence: CRUD + filtering + screenshots and run steps in the README.
projects.p3_desc: Agenda app to manage contacts and/or events with a clean, productivity-focused UI.
projects.p3_why: It helped me practice app structure, data persistence and a clean UI designed for real usage.
projects.p3_problem: Managing contacts/tasks per user and keeping data safe and accessible across devices.
projects.p3_solution: Android app in Kotlin with Firebase Auth + Realtime Database, CRUD and UI validations/feedback.
projects.p3_result: Evidence: login/register + per-user cloud CRUD + screenshots in the repo.
projects.p4_desc: Real-time collaborative bingo: multiple users join a room and the board state syncs instantly.
projects.p4_why: Previously called “BingoEnvidiosos”. Great practice for real-time sync, shared state and multi-user UX.
projects.p4_problem: Coordinating a shared board across multiple users in real time without desync or page reloads.
projects.p4_solution: Room-based web app with real-time shared state, handling events and consistency across clients.
projects.p4_result: Evidence: real-time multi-user project (repo includes features and structure).
projects.p5_desc: Automated E2E tests to validate real user flows on web, making sure key features don’t break.
projects.p5_why: It builds discipline: reproducible tests, early bug detection and a quality-first mindset.
projects.p5_problem: Catching breaking changes in critical user flows before they hit production.
projects.p5_solution: Selenium + JUnit5 suite using Page Objects, wait helpers and automated execution in CI.
projects.p5_result: Evidence: CI + reporting (Allure) + execution video in the repo.
projects.p6_desc: A set of Kotlin mini-projects to master key areas: multimedia, concurrency and persistence.
projects.p6_why: Mini-case format: a real problem, a concrete solution and a clear competency signal.
projects.p6_problem: Learning key Kotlin/Android concepts fast without getting stuck in huge slow-to-iterate projects.
projects.p6_result: Evidence: 3 repos with features + screenshots/docs per mini-case.
projects.p7_desc: 100% local pipeline to turn PDFs into a searchable RAG knowledge base (answers with citations) and automate ingestion + daily digests with n8n.
projects.p7_why: It helped me build a full end-to-end system: ingest → page extraction → embeddings → semantic search → answers with sources, fully local, with a secured API (JWT).
projects.p7_problem: When you pile up PDFs (guides, notes, specs), finding reliable answers is slow and hard to trace.
projects.p7_solution: Local stack with n8n workflows, Spring Boot API (JWT), Postgres + pgvector, and Ollama for embeddings + RAG returning `sources[]` with page/snippet evidence.
projects.p7_result: Evidence: `/ask` returns an answer + cited sources/pages; WF1 ingests PDFs from `inbox/` and WF2 writes daily digests to `outbox/` (docs + Postman collection).
projects.p8_desc: Personal system for habits + gamification (XP/HP/streaks) + daily logging + digital detox, with Notion as the base and automation on top.
projects.p8_why: A big end-to-end project: I connect real components (Notion + Make + ntfy + Android) and document everything so it stays maintainable and robust.
projects.p8_problem: I wanted a single system to track habits and digital detox without paid apps or daily manual work.
projects.p8_solution: Notion data model + daily Make scenario for streaks/XP/HP + push notifications via ntfy + Android Detox app exporting CSV by app/category.
projects.p8_result: Evidence: 0€ functional system (Notion/Make free) with docs, daily automation, and CSV export feeding the detox module.
